column1: What three competing constraints does Next.js's rendering strategy decomposition (SSG/SSR/ISR/CSR) fundamentally reconcile?
column2: Time-to-first-byte latency budget, JavaScript bundle size transmitted over the network, and the computational cost of hydrating a static DOM into an interactive React tree.

column1: What key architectural insight allows React Server Components to eliminate JavaScript from the client bundle?
column2: Most components are purely presentational data transformations (e.g., mapping DB rows to HTML) that don't require client-side interactivity, so they can execute on the server and stream serialized output instead of shipping JS.

column1: How does the RSC wire protocol transmit Server Component output to the client?
column2: As a streaming, compact JSON-like serialization of React elements, props, and async suspense boundaries, sent over HTTP chunked transfer encoding.

column1: In the App Router, where does data fetching occur relative to the Pages Router model?
column2: Pages Router: one page = one getServerSideProps/getStaticProps waterfall at the page boundary. App Router: every Server Component in the tree can independently await its own data, coordinated by React's concurrent rendering and fetch deduplication.

column1: Why does filesystem-based routing enable build-time optimization that imperative routers (e.g., Express.js) cannot?
column2: Because the URL space is isomorphic to the directory tree, the compiler can statically traverse it, classify every route as static/dynamic, and derive the full rendering strategy before any request arrives—impossible when routes are registered imperatively at runtime.

column1: What is the memory ceiling typically imposed on a V8 Isolate executing Next.js Middleware at the edge?
Which Node.js capabilities are forbidden inside the Next.js Edge Runtime, and how is this enforced?
column2: No `fs` module, arbitrary TCP sockets, `child_process`, or native addons. Enforcement is a compile-time invariant: the bundler verifies no imported module transitively requires a Node.js built-in, failing the build if one is found.

column1: What web-standard APIs remain available within the Next.js Edge Runtime?
column2: fetch, Request, Response, URL, Headers, ReadableStream, crypto.subtle, TextEncoder, and a small set of other web platform APIs.

column1: Why can a V8 Isolate start in under a millisecond compared to a full Node.js process?
column2: It is a lightweight, sandboxed JS execution context that avoids spinning up a full Node.js event loop, allocating heap for a module registry, or establishing long-lived connections to a central process manager.

column1: What happens when a server component attempts to pass a function or class instance to a client component across the serialization boundary?
column2: It triggers a runtime exception, because the server/client boundary is opaque and uni-directional, supporting only serializable data.

column1: What is the consequence of exceeding a serverless function's execution duration or memory ceiling in a Next.js deployment?
column2: Abrupt request termination with a 504 Gateway Timeout response, not graceful degradation.

column1: What are the three immutable invariants of Next.js production readiness described in the deployment lesson?
column2: 1) Every page's server-rendered HTML, client hydration payload, and static artifact must maintain semantic equivalence or hydration mismatches occur. 2) Server and client components inhabit separate execution contexts with an opaque, uni-directional serialization boundary. 3) Serverless functions operate under strict resource constraints (duration, memory, cold-start) whose violation causes abrupt failure.
